'''Configurational mechanics''' is a subdiscipline of [[continuum mechanics]] in which particular emphasis is placed on reckoning from the perspective of the material [[manifold]].  By contrast, in [[classical mechanics]], reckoning is commonly made from the perspective of [[spatial coordinates]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kienzler |first1=R. |last2=Maugin |first2=G. A. |title=Configurational mechanics of materials (Vol. 427) |date=2002 |publisher=Springer}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Steinmann |first1=P. |title=On boundary potential energies in deformational and configurational mechanics. |journal=Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids |date=2008 |volume=56 |issue=3 |pages=772–800|doi=10.1016/j.jmps.2007.07.001 |bibcode=2008JMPSo..56..772S }}</ref>

Configurational mechanics has been applied to the analysis of [[Fracture mechanics|crack growth]]. In these applications, growth of the crack corresponds to a material [[Displacement (geometry)|displacement]], and the configurational force causing crack growth emerges as the [[Energy release rate]].
<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Verron |first1=E. |title=Configurational mechanics: a tool to investigate fracture and fatigue of rubber. |journal=Rubber Chemistry and Technology |date=2010 |volume=83 |issue=3 |pages=270–281|doi=10.5254/1.3525685 |s2cid=138329716 |url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-01005989/file/EVC.pdf }}</ref>
